nodes.source_text: Figure 1A shows the response to methanol observed on Ni, Co, and Fe, three representative catalysts for OER with different OER reactivity. nodes.description: OER performance variation with Fe content in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: By increasing the content of Fe in Ni-Fe film until optimum, the anodic peak shifts positively while OER onset shifts negatively (Figures 5 and S15)

nodes.description: OER performance in acidic medium with alcohol probe
nodes.source_text: An investigation over IrO2 with our method shows similar results in acidic medium as well (Figure S14), where obvious but relatively small alcohol oxidation current can be observed. However, a detailed comparison of RRDE tests for IrO2 in alkaline and acidic media shows that OER is suppressed more seriously by alcohol in acid

nodes.description: MOR and OER comparison with NiO
nodes.source_text: We conducted a direct comparison between LaNiO3 and NiO with our method (Figure S5), while experimental results do not support the metal redox theory... lower overpotential of MOR is observed on NiO and higher OER activity is seen on LaNiO3

nodes.characterization_summary: CV curves show typical redox peaks prior to OER onset on Ni and Co (oxy)hydroxides, no faradic process except OER on Fe (oxy)hydroxide; methanol addition causes irreversible oxidation current on Ni from anodic peak onset, plateau at OER onset.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1A shows the response to methanol observed on Ni, Co, and Fe, three representative catalysts for OER... In a pure KOH electrolyte, typical redox peaks are observable on Ni and Co prior to the onset of OER current, while no faradic process is discernable on Fe except for OER current, in line with the kinetic feature reported in literature.

nodes.characterization_summary: LSV in 1 M KOH with/without methanol shows MOR current indicating OH* surface coverage trend: NiO > Co3O4 > IrO2, no OH* adsorption detected on Fe2O3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Figure 3, MOR current indicates that the surface coverage of OH* varies in the trend: NiO > Co3O4 > IrO2, while no OH* could be adsorbed on Fe2O3 (hematite).

nodes.characterization_summary: RRDE Tafel plots of IrO2 in 1M (KOH + MeOH) show disk Tafel slope 110.5 mV/dec at low current (alcohol oxidation dominant), changing to ~60 mV/dec at high current where OER dominates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: On disk electrode, a high Tafel slope (110.5 mV/dec) is clearly observable in a low-current region where alcohol oxidation dominates, while it changes to lower value (about 60 mV/dec) at a high current.
